correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts Ω≤2, including primes, squares and products of two distinct primes, with 1 checked separately. Equality σ(n)=σ(n+1) excludes prime endpoints; the even composite is necessarily 2p with odd prime p (the exceptional 4 has prime neighbors). The odd neighbor is q² or qr. For q² and odd squarefree qr, each of the two orientations produces respectively (q−1)²=0, q²−2q+7=0, (q−2)(r−2)=3, or (q−2)(r−2)=−3. For primes 3≤q<r, only the third is solvable, q=3, r=5, p=7, yielding n=14. Independent divisor sums σ(14)=σ(15)=24 are exact. The finite sieve cited by the package is corroboration, not the proof.

value.rationale: The lowest nontrivial composite layer (two prime factors counted with multiplicity on each consecutive integer) is a canonical multiplicative-complexity boundary in the classical unsolved divisor-sum equality problem. The all-integers classification identifies the entire minimal Ω stratum and provides a precise first structural exclusion for further searches, rather than arbitrarily checking to a numerical cutoff. Its short elementary argument does not make it an arbitrary or previously implied computation.

limitations: Theorem classifies only simultaneous Ω≤2; higher Ω layers and the infinitude question remain untouched.
An obscure prior elementary classification remains a bibliographic residual risk.
